requirement:
`habeas status` MUST look up, under {cite}`requirements.authoring.github_reads`,
every issue that a `:github:` option line of a named or unnamed `{fixme}` under
{cite}`requirements.references.roles` names, and MUST report each `{fixme}`
naming an issue that is closed or does not exist as an error, with its file and
line and the issue. It MUST also report the item that contains that `{fixme}` as
failing: the outline node containing it, or the requirement or example
declaration whose body contains it, in the same way it reports an uncovered
Rust item. When GitHub cannot be reached, the issue MUST be assumed open.
Repository validation MUST NOT contact GitHub.
rationale:
structural: I found no structural obligation in `requirements.cli.fixme_issues` that needs implementation evidence. Every clause specifies observable behavior of `habeas status`, so there are no implementation roots to assess.

- "MUST look up, under `requirements.authoring.github_reads`, every issue that a `:github:` option line ... names". This requires every named issue to be looked up. An implementation that fetched the issues in a different order, or through different internal functions, would behave the same and still comply. The one-cache rule belongs to the cited `requirements.authoring.github_reads`, which is context here and not part of this subject's text.
- "MUST report each `{fixme}` naming an issue that is closed or does not exist as an error, with its file and line and the issue". This is output content. No type, signature or library is prescribed.
- "MUST also report the item that contains that `{fixme}` as failing ... in the same way it reports an uncovered Rust item". This is a reporting outcome. It does not prescribe how the code is organized or which interface it delegates to.
- "When GitHub cannot be reached, the issue MUST be assumed open". This is a decision about behavior. It names no structure.
- "Repository validation MUST NOT contact GitHub". This is a behavioral prohibition.

I could not construct a behavior-preserving alternative that violates any clause. So none of the clauses is a structural obligation, and the empty set of roots is correct.

behavioral: The reviewed tests cover each obligation of `requirements.cli.fixme_issues`.

**Lookup of every issue named by a `:github:` line in a named or unnamed `{fixme}`.**
- `src/github.rs#mod[tests]/fn[closed_and_missing_issues_fail_their_fixmes_items_and_acknowledged_records]` uses the `project()` fixture. In it, a named `{fixme}` in the Rust source has two `:github:` lines (one closed issue and one open issue).
- The same test has unnamed `{fixme}`s in a requirement body and in an appended example body, both naming an issue that does not exist.
- It asserts that the open issue yields no error, which shows each issue is looked up and judged separately.

**Error for a closed or nonexistent issue, with file, line and issue.**
- The test asserts the exact messages for the closed issue in the Rust file and the nonexistent issue in the chapter file. Each gives file, line and issue.
- The exact total count of added errors rules out spurious or duplicate findings.

**Containing item reported as failing.**
- For the outline node, it asserts the `fn ready fails: its {fixme} ...` message.
- For requirement and example declarations, it asserts the `requirement rules.ready fails: ...` message and the `example rules.unfinished fails: its {fixme} ...` message.
- `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[closing_an_acknowledged_issue_makes_the_fixme_record_stale_and_reassessed]` checks the same kinds of messages through the real `habeas status` command, including `fn beta fails` and an `Invalid` row.

**GitHub unreachable means the issue is assumed open.**
- The unit test runs `GithubIssues::offline()` and an unreachable local port. In both cases the errors are unchanged from before.

**Lookups go through the cache under `requirements.authoring.github_reads`.**
- The integration test checks that the cache file exists under the state root.
- It checks that a changed remote state is not seen while the cache is fresh and that the request count stays the same.
- It checks that after the cache file is removed exactly one new read happens and the closed state is reported.

**Repository validation MUST NOT contact GitHub.**
- The unit test asserts the read count is zero after `inspect_repository`.
- The integration test asserts that `habeas::validate_repository` reports no errors and that the request count is unchanged.

`src/inputs.rs#mod[tests]/fn[yaml_sequence_entry_reports_its_dash_as_the_declaration_line]` only supports the line and outline-owner mapping. It is not needed for any other obligation.

I found no untested obligation and no wrong assertion.

text: :::{req} fixme_issues
`habeas status` MUST look up, under {cite}`requirements.authoring.github_reads`,
every issue that a `:github:` option line of a named or unnamed `{fixme}` under
{cite}`requirements.references.roles` names, and MUST report each `{fixme}`
naming an issue that is closed or does not exist as an error, with its file and
line and the issue. It MUST also report the item that contains that `{fixme}` as
failing: the outline node containing it, or the requirement or example
declaration whose body contains it, in the same way it reports an uncovered
Rust item. When GitHub cannot be reached, the issue MUST be assumed open.
Repository validation MUST NOT contact GitHub.
:::{req} github_reads
The harness MUST expose a `github` tool with this interface:
```text
github({ issue: String }) -> Issue
Issue { reference: String, state: "open" | "closed", title: String, body: String }
`issue` MUST have the form `<owner>/<repo>#<number>`. The tool MUST read the issue
or pull request through the GitHub API, authenticating with the `GITHUB_TOKEN`
environment variable when that is set, and MUST return its body redacted under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.redaction`. GitHub reads cannot be reproduced
later, so their results MUST NOT be recorded as evidence inputs and MUST NOT
make evidence stale. Every GitHub read by Habeas, including this tool's, the
lookups below, and those of {cite}`requirements.cli.fixme_issues`, MUST go
through one cache under the state root of
{cite}`requirements.configuration.state_location`, keyed by issue, and MUST
reuse a cached result less than one hour old instead of contacting GitHub. A malformed reference, a missing issue, or a failed request
MUST return an explanatory tool error.
When the mandatory inputs contain a `{fixme}` reference under
{cite}`requirements.references.roles`, or the initial request includes one under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.fixme_inputs`, the harness MUST look up the state of
each issue its `:github:` lines name in the same way and MUST supply each state
with the corresponding source input or acknowledgment as `open` or `closed`;
when GitHub cannot be reached, the issue MUST be assumed open. These states MUST

NOT be recorded either. Instead, `habeas status` and `habeas author` MUST treat a recorded FIXME determination as stale, exactly as if one of its inputs had changed, when an issue that one of its acknowledging `{fixme}` references names, or for a site review the `{fixme}` references inside the site, is closed or does not exist; repository validation, which never contacts GitHub, MUST NOT.
The harness MAY take the GitHub API base URL from `HABEAS_GITHUB_API_URL`,
accepting only `http://127.0.0.1:<port>`, so that tests can use a local server.
:::{req} roles

Project text files MAY use the `{impl}`, `{cite}`, and `{test}` roles with a backtick-delimited full requirement or example name, or with a built-in name under {cite}`requirements.references.builtin_definitions`, and MAY use the `{fixme}` role in fenced form. A reference MAY instead be written in fenced form, `:::{role} name` on one line, a body, and a closing fence, following the fence rules of {cite}`requirements.ci.span` and {cite}`requirements.ci.fence_lengths`; the fenced form is the same edge with attached commentary, and the inline form carries none. In a source comment, fence lines MUST be recognized after removing each line's comment delimiters within one comment run under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`, and a fence that does not close within its comment run MUST be a validation error. Each reference is a directed edge between its source and the named definition. A source is a {term}`requirements.references.source_item` or a requirement or example declaration. The roles MUST mean:
- `{cite}`: the source relies on, supports, or refers to the definition. It is an
edge from the source to the definition.
- `{impl}`: the source implements part of the definition: it makes a decision,
performs a check, produces an output, or handles a case that the definition
specifies. A requirement MAY implement part of another requirement by refining
one of its obligations. Calling code that implements a definition, or
producing a result a caller uses to meet it, MUST NOT by itself count as
implementing it. A check MUST count only if the definition states it, or the
source could not meet one of the definition's obligations without it; source
that checks it is consistent with a definition, such as recognizing a form the
definition specifies in order to decide whether to run other behavior, relies
on that definition and calls for `{cite}`. A requirement stating a convention
for every output of a kind, such as every validation error, is implemented by
the source that carries out the convention as a whole, such as the step that
collects and reports those outputs.
- `{test}`: the source is designed to verify behavior the definition specifies:
a test through its scenario and the assertions about that scenario's outcome,
or a named example through the concrete case it describes.
- `{fixme}`: the source acknowledges a known gap in fulfilling the definition. It
MUST use the fenced form, and its body MUST describe the gap. The body MAY
begin with option lines naming issues that track the gap, one per line, in the
form `:github: <owner>/<repo>#<number>`, such as
`:github: rust-lang/rust#123`. `github` MUST be the only recognized option.
A named `{fixme}` MAY appear only in sources outside the book. Validation MUST report
any other option line, a `:github:` value not in that form, an inline
`{fixme}`, a `{fixme}` in a requirement or example declaration, and a
`{fixme}` whose body, without option lines and comment delimiters, is empty.
An unnamed `{fixme}`, a fence of `:::{fixme}` with no name, MAY appear in any
project text, including a requirement or example body, to tie that place to
the issues it names. It MUST have at least one `:github:` option line and MAY
have a description; it is not a reference edge, acknowledges no gap, and needs
no evidence input. Its issues are checked under {cite}`requirements.cli.fixme_issues`.
`{impl}`, `{test}`, and `{fixme}` are edges from the definition to the source.
Code implementations are reviewed as part of the definitions they implement or
test. Citation reviews assess cited source items and book passages under
{cite}`requirements.references.citation_review`.
```text
{impl}`requirements.references.roles`
{cite}`requirements.references.roles`
{test}`requirements.references.roles`
:::{definition} source_item
:phrase: source item
A node in a project file’s outline, identified by the project-relative path
and an outline selector. For example, `src/auth.rs#fn[check_token]` identifies
a Rust function. The root node represents the whole file. A reference in a
comment belongs to the item that owns the comment under
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_comments`.
